title: Repair an interval check
prompt: Write `public static bool InWindow(int value, int start, int end)`. The interval includes start and excludes end. When start is equal to or greater than end, it is empty. Save the starter and use the failed checks to find both boundary mistakes.
hints: Compare values just below, exactly at, and just above each end.
The start belongs to the interval, but the end does not.
Use value >= start && value < end. This also makes an empty or reversed interval false.
checkLabels: A value between the boundaries must be included.
A value below the start must be excluded.
A value above the end must be excluded.
Equal boundaries give an empty interval.
Reversed boundaries give an empty interval.
Negative boundaries follow the same rule.

wrongAnswers.misconception: Includes both boundaries, so the excluded end passes.
Excludes both boundaries, so the included start fails.

feedback: Trace the start and end separately. Then check an empty interval and negative values.
